nonvacuity: scratch/Checks.lean compiles examples placing observed121 in both supports and alternative121 in unrestricted121. There are no theorem premises. The swap has block counts 6 and 54, so it genuinely leaves the blocked support; the two fixed four-node outcomes are assignment-independent sharp-null outcomes and both tails are genuine finite probabilities.

scratch/SpatialNonvacuity.lean compiles an example satisfying every spatial-clause hypothesis simultaneously: N=2 distinct nodes at (0,0),(1,0), field the whole plane, measure the sum of Dirac masses there, Y identically zero, D={0}, Q uniform on all two-node assignments, A={treatedCount=1}, and delta=1/20. Positive conditional support has one node in each arm, every circle mass is one, all outcomes are integrable, and sigma-finiteness is checked. scratch/Checks.lean also constructs a common-Bernoulli(1/2) law and computes its positive count-two event probability 3/8.

The assertion supplies its fixed witness and has no premise making that witness conditional. Its bounded Borel outcomes on the rectangle satisfy the sharp null everywhere; each evaluated circle has one atom and two nonempty treatment arms. scratch/Checks.lean independently compiles all six Hajek values, both type-7 endpoints, the exact rejection probability 1/3, a genuine independent-Bernoulli(1/2) law, and its count-two probability 3/8. The geometric and measure checks are detailed in REPORT.md.

scratch/Checks.lean compiles a nonconstant contrast for y=(0,1,2,3), the level bounds at delta=1/20, and a genuine IID instance with Q uniform on Fin 2, B=2, and R uniform on all functions Fin 3 -> Fin 2, proving the product-mass hypothesis for every array. Nonempty rejection sets exist (for example {0}); no inconsistent hypothesis is used.

The fixed two-node witness has no supplied hypotheses. scratch/Checks.lean compiles its exact nonempty circles, both actual circle-mean formulas on all four assignments, and the covariance 1/4 of its actual linearization scores. For the universal replication clauses M=1 is admissible; for every M>0 the full Boolean function law is independent fair assignment, each circle is the two endpoints, and the independent-pair sign calculation gives variance 1/(4M) versus cutoff covariance sum 1/(8M), as detailed in REPORT.md. No actual Hajek ratio on an empty arm is evaluated.
